project.name: Tic-Tac-Toe Coach
project.summary: A one-page web app that plays tic-tac-toe with a child and teaches them to win: a coach at three strengths, a Help me button that rings the best square and says why, and two children on one phone. It speaks English, Hebrew and Polish, keeps everything on the phone, and is published on GitHub Pages.

nodes.summary: The pieces of the app, kept as separate files while you work on them and glued into one page for publishing.

nodes.label: The coach's brains
nodes.summary: Knows the game inside out: who has won, the best square from any position, the true reason for a hint, how each of the three coaches plays, and why the child lost.

nodes.label: Words in three languages

links.desc: The screens ask the coach for its move, for the best square when Help me is tapped, and for why the child lost.
Every word on screen is looked up in the words table, in the language the child picked.
The build reads the CSS and JavaScript pieces in src, in a fixed order.
The build pours the pieces into the page template and writes index.html.
GitHub Pages serves the committed index.html to phones.
The test loader reads the source files straight from src and runs them in Node, with no browser.
Playwright opens the built index.html in a phone-sized headless Chromium.
The page template links the typefaces from Google Fonts; phones download only the scripts they render.

flows.title: A game against the coach
flows.description: From the welcome screen to the end of a game.

steps.note: The child picks Single player, the coach's level, X or O and who starts, taps Play, then taps a square.
After a short wait the coach picks its square at the chosen level (Easy slips, Medium always wins and blocks, Hard never loses) and names its reason.
The coach's square gets a magenta ring and its one line appears under the board, in the child's language.
If the coach won, it looks back over the game for the child's missed win, missed block, or the two ways to win that beat them.
The end of the game: confetti for a win, a handshake for a draw, a grey rainy screen for a loss, and Play again.

flows.title: Help me
flows.description: How the coach shows the best square and says why.

steps.note: The child taps Help me on their turn.
Works out every best square, then the first reason that is true of one: win now, block, two ways to win, two in a row, stop their two ways, the middle, a corner, any square, a side.
Rings that square in pulsing magenta and puts the reason in the box. The child may still play anywhere.

flows.title: From a change to the live site

steps.note: Edit a piece in src. npm test checks the coach and the words straight from the pieces.
python3 build.py glues the pieces into index.html.
The browser tests play the built page in three languages; index.html is committed with the sources.
A push to main is live within a minute.

tasks.title: The first version
tasks.request: Build Tic-Tac-Toe Coach from the approved design, then open it locally for me to test
tasks.summary: The whole app was built in 13 reviewed steps: a coach at three strengths, Help me with a true reason, two players on one phone, three languages, and the end-of-game screens with confetti, a handshake and a grey day. Everything is checked by quick checks and browser tests in all three languages.

tasks.title: The board stays put
tasks.request: When the game finishes the whole game moves up a bit; the board shouldn't move
tasks.summary: The end-of-game screens now keep the same title and line above the board as the play screen, the handshake sits inside the draw's title, and the board keeps its size. The board's top is the same while playing and after the game, in all three languages.

tasks.title: No taps while the coach thinks
tasks.request: It's clickable while the coach thinks; it shouldn't be
tasks.summary: During the coach's short wait every empty square is switched off, so it neither presses nor takes a tap, and the squares come back as soon as the coach has moved.

items.note: New: the coach itself. It finds the best square from any position, gives a reason that is always true, plays Easy, Medium and Hard, and explains a loss, which is what teaches the child to win.
New: the three screens you approved from the mockups, the coach's turn after a short wait, Help me's ring, and the game saved on the phone so a reload lands on the same board.
New: every word the child reads, in English, Hebrew and Polish, side by side so you can review them in one place.
New: the look you picked: blue X and orange O, the magenta rings that belong to the coach, the handshake and the grey rainy loss screen.
New: starts the app in the phone's language with the setup you used last, so the usual path is one tap on Play.
New: proves the Hard coach never loses and that a child who follows every hint never loses either.
New: plays whole games in a phone-sized browser in all three languages, including reloads, two players and the loss screen.
New: walks every screen in each language and checks it fits a small phone without scrolling.
The end-of-game screen keeps the line under the title that the play screen has, so nothing above the board changes height when the game ends.
The handshake now sits inside the draw's title instead of pushing the board down, and the rule that shrank the board on a draw is gone.
Now fails if the board's top differs between the play screen and any end-of-game screen, in each language.
Checks the board's position and size before and after a win, a draw and a loss.
Switches the empty squares off for the coach's turn and back on after its move, and gives a keyboard player their square back.
A switched-off square no longer shows the press effect or the pointing hand.
Checks every empty square is off right after the child's move and on again once the coach has played.
